subject: Latency SLO commitments for Hosted API — clarification and proposed exception
messages:
From: Liza Morales <liza.morales@acadiahealth.com>
To: grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Acadia Health Procurement <procurement@acadiahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Aug 2025 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API latency SLO — P50/P95 and measurement window details

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the product overview yesterday. As part of our procurement checklist we need explicit SLO language for the hosted API in the contract. Two quick asks we need clarified before legal will approve:

1) Exact numeric targets for P50 and P95 (we need numbers, e.g., 50ms / 200ms).
2) How you measure those numbers — rolling window (30d?), percentile calculation method, and what request population is included (all requests vs. production-only).

We also have a high-throughput use case (batching on our side + heavy prompt KV cache) and would like an exception/commitment if the p95 is breached repeatedly during the first 90 days after go-live. If you offer a ramp or credit, please state the terms.

Attached is our standard SLA questionnaire (we filled the non-Redwood portions). Can you return a proposed clause we can send to legal?

Best,
Liza Morales
Sr. Procurement Manager, Acadia Health
Acadia Health

Attachments: Acadia_SLA_Questionnaire.xlsx (XLSX)

From: grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Liza Morales <liza.morales@acadiahealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>; neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Aug 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API latency SLO — P50/P95 and measurement window details

Hi Liza — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise draft we can include in the contract; I've looped in Marissa (Sales Lead) and Neha (Product) to confirm operations and credit terms.

Proposed Hosted API Latency SLO (draft):
- Measurement population: production requests addressed to customer-specific tenant routes (excluding synthetic test traffic and known maintenance windows).
- Measurement method: rolling 30‑day window; percentiles computed over aggregated end-to-end server-side response times (server receive -> final token emitted).
- Targets: P50 <= 60 ms, P95 <= 250 ms.
- Exception / ramp: For initial 90 days post-go-live, Redwood may operate under a soft ramp where P95 target is provisionally 300 ms (to allow tuning of batching/VM sizing). If P95 > 250 ms for 3+ non-consecutive days within any 30-day window after the ramp, Redwood will issue a service credit equal to 5% of that month's invoice for each full day of breach, capped at 25% for the calendar month.

We can tighten the provisional P95 (e.g., to 220 ms) if Acadia commits to enabling Redwood prefix caching and follows basic batching best-practices we recommend — happy to include a short technical appendix.

I'll attach a draft SLA clause and a short measurement methodology doc for legal/ops. If that looks ok, I can route to Legal for an official addendum and include the DocuSign link.

Cheers,
Grace O'Connor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: SLA_draft_Acadia.pdf (PDF), latency-measurement-methodology.docx (DOCX)

From: grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Aug 2025 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Hosted API latency SLO — internal approval needed

Marissa / Neha — forwarding Liza's request + my proposed draft (see attachments). Key asks for approval:

- Do we feel comfortable offering P50 60ms / P95 250ms as the baseline?
- For the 90-day ramp, is provisional P95=300ms acceptable or should we promise a lower interim number?
- Credit formula: I proposed 5% per breach day capped at 25%/month. Approve?

Notes: customer is a healthcare provider (PHI considerations), likely to push for stronger SLAs. They will probably enable caching but we should not require it as a hard precondition. Happy to take this to Legal once we lock numbers.

Thanks,
Grace

--Forwarded message follows--

From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Aug 2025 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Hosted API latency SLO — internal approval needed

Grace / Neha — I reviewed the proposed numbers. My recommendations:

- Baseline targets: keep P50 <= 60 ms, adjust P95 to <= 220 ms for the contractual target. 220 ms is a better marketing/enterprise signal and achievable on our hosted fleet for typical cardiology/patient‑lookup workloads.
- Ramp: offer a 90‑day ramp with provisional P95 = 270 ms (not 300). This gives ops room to tune without a big perceived downgrade.
- Credits: 5% per day of breach is fine, cap at 20%/month. Also add a clause that credits do not apply if breach is caused by customer misconfiguration, customer network issues, or scheduled maintenance with 48h notice.
- Operational requirement: we should include an appendix listing recommended tuning steps (prefix caching, recommended batch sizes, region pinning). We can make these "best-effort recommendations" rather than hard preconditions.

If you both sign off I'll approve for Legal routing. Good job drafting.

Marissa Cole
Director, Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Liza Morales <liza.morales@acadiahealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Acadia Health Procurement <procurement@acadiahealth.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Aug 2025 16:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Final proposed latency SLO clause and next steps

Hi Liza — thanks for the patience while we finalized internally. Below is the final language Redwood is prepared to include in the contract; we added a short appendix with tuning recommendations (attached).

Final Proposed Clause (summary):
- Measurement population: production tenant-specific requests.
- Measurement window: rolling 30-day window. Percentiles calculated over server-side end-to-end response times.
- Contractual targets: P50 <= 60 ms; P95 <= 220 ms.
- Initial ramp: first 90 days post-go-live, provisional P95 = 270 ms.
- Credits: If after the ramp period P95 > 220 ms for 3 or more non-consecutive days in any 30-day window, Redwood will issue a service credit equal to 5% of that month's Redwood invoice for each full day of breach, capped at 20% for that month. Credits do not apply to outages caused by Customer network issues, customer misconfigurations, force majeure, or scheduled maintenance with 48 hours' notice.

Operational appendix (attached): recommended prefix/KV caching settings, suggested batch sizes, and region pinning options to meet P95 targets. If Acadia agrees to implement the recommendations within 30 days of go-live, Redwood will commit to an operational review at day 30 and a target tuning pass with priority scheduling.

Next steps: if this is acceptable, we'll send the SLA addendum to your legal team via DocuSign and include the attachments. I can also schedule a 30-minute ops call to walk through the tuning appendix.

Best,
